title: Continuous Integration and Automated Checks
learning_outcomes: Describe the purpose and main behavior of continuous integration and automated checks.
Apply continuous integration and automated checks in a small Python example or interpret a representative result.
Identify one limitation, edge case, compatibility concern, or failure mode relevant to the topic.

content.intro: This lesson introduces continuous integration and automated checks as part of professional python development and deployment. It turns the curriculum heading into a short, practical concept guide with a visual, example, and checks to try locally.
content.why_it_matters: Professional work is reproducible and observable. Separate configuration from code, test important failures, document setup, and verify the exact deployed runtime.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Professional work is reproducible and observable. Separate configuration from code, test important failures, document setup, and verify the exact deployed runtime.

content_blocks.title: How to work with it
content_blocks.text: For continuous integration and automated checks, identify the inputs and assumptions first. Use the smallest useful example, predict its behavior, run it in a local Python interpreter, and compare the observed result with your prediction. The example below is a static reference in CodeLeaf, not executed Python.
